note: Literature confirms FBXO11-related disorder is characterized by static neurodevelopmental delay rather than neurodegeneration, lacks major structural malformations like limb reductions, and typically exhibits mild microcephaly (24%) or macrocephaly rather than profound microcephaly.

evidence.text: In a cohort of 21 individuals with FBXO11 variants, microcephaly was present in only 24%, neuroimaging findings were nonspecific, and presentation centered on mild ID and subtle dysmorphism without progressive neurodegeneration.

source.title: Defining FBXO11-Related Neurodevelopmental Disorder: Clinical, Molecular and Facial Assessment of 21 Patients
source.quote: Mild intellectual disability (86%), facial dysmorphism (67%), hypotonia (62%), and behavioural dysregulation (62%) were the most prevalent features. Microcephaly occurred in 24%, while seizures were present in 43%. Brain imaging abnormalities were nonspecific

evidence.text: In 12 Chinese individuals across 5 families with FBXO11 variants, major structural malformations were not observed, supporting the absence of gross structural birth defects such as limb reduction anomalies.

source.title: FBXO11 variants are associated with intellectual disability and variable clinical manifestation in Chinese affected individuals
source.quote: Distinguishingly, malformation was not observed in all the affected individuals.
